summary: The path-tracing OOM fix and the sleeper night shots are plausible and cheap, but the last suite run (58/59) still fails on the follow camera test, and the author's journal says a different test failed. Unresolved.

findings.what: The last host suite run fails 'The follow camera shows its creature big (>=15%)': Sprout fills only 10%. The tester says the camera was following a moment subject (a crab in a party hat at ~35%) while the test measures Sprout. The journal blames a flaky Night shots test and does not mention this failure. Night shots and sleeper framing changes may have changed which creature the camera picks.
findings.evidence: results/session-0034.json: failed=[follow camera ... 'Sprout fills only 10.0%']; tests/shots/follow_big.png
findings.suggestion: Make the test measure the creature the camera is actually framing (or force no moment subject), and confirm the night/sleeper shots do not make the follow camera drop Sprout when a player is controlling it.

findings.what: The sleeper night-shot fix only works because beds.jl relocates beds to the crown edge. The author admits most critters otherwise sleep under crowns, and the evidence is forced shots. #168 and #175 (path tracing during the firefly game) are still open or untested live.
findings.suggestion: Watch a real night in the live game and add a before/after check. Try path tracing during a firefly round before closing #175.

findings.what: The 'On the island now' panel is new UI, but the engine's changelog line under Sprout is still left, and the panel text was not checked at the dashboard's size.
findings.suggestion: Check the panel's legibility in the live dashboard and remove the leftover changelog line in the next engine batch.

response: s35: the follow-camera size test measured interesting_subject at one instant while the camera was still framing the previous moment subject (the party crab). The test now waits until the camera has watched one creature for 3 s and skips group moments (CAMERA_GROUPS, tested by their plugins); passes live. The other two findings stay open as todos #168/#175 (night framing, path tracing during firefly) and #174 (engine changelog line).
